title: Infant baptism can be proved from Scripture — Bellarmine refutes Anabaptists, then denies the proof
source_text: XXIII. Objiciunt praeterea, Bellarminus & alii, baptismum parvulorum tanquam rem necessariam, & tamen in sacra Scriptura non traditam, aut saltem quae sufficienter non probetur ex sacra Scriptura. Sed negamus non posse ex sacra Scriptura probari legitimum esse baptismum infantium. Illud certe multis & validis argumentis ex Scriptura sacra deductis contra Anabaptistas Theologi nostri confirmant. Quae argumenta referre & vindicare hujus loci non esset, & prolixiorem operam requirit. Sed quod valde mirum est, ipsi Pontificii ex Scripturis Anabaptistas egregie confutant. Inter alios vero Bellarminus de hac controversia ex Scripturis ita disputat, ut argumenta sua, nulla ratione solvi, nulla arte eludi posse, glorietur & fidat, libr. 1. de sacram. Bapt. cap. 9. Et tamen idem ille sui oblitus, dum Scripturae sufficientiam impugnare conatur, asserit paedobaptismum ex Scriptura satis probare non posse. Sed hic a Bellarmino studio causae abrepto, ad Bellarminum alibi evidentia veritatis convictum appellamus.
pass_a_gloss: Besides, Bellarmine and others object infant baptism as a necessary matter, and yet not handed down in sacred Scripture, or at least not sufficiently proved from sacred Scripture. But we deny that it cannot be proved from sacred Scripture that the baptism of infants is legitimate. That certainly our theologians confirm against the Anabaptists by many and strong arguments drawn from sacred Scripture. To recite and vindicate those arguments would not belong to this place, and requires longer labor. But what is greatly wonderful is that the Pontiffs themselves egregiously refute the Anabaptists from the Scriptures. Among others Bellarmine so disputes this controversy from the Scriptures that he boasts and trusts that his arguments can by no reason be solved, by no art eluded — book 1 On the Sacrament of Baptism, chapter 9. And yet the same man, forgetting himself, while he tries to assail Scripture's sufficiency, asserts that paedobaptism cannot be sufficiently proved from Scripture. But here from Bellarmine carried away by zeal for his cause we appeal to Bellarmine elsewhere convinced by the evidence of the truth.
pass_b_english: They next call infant baptism necessary yet unwritten — or at least not proved enough from Scripture.
We deny the silence: our theologians prove infant baptism from Scripture against the Anabaptists.
This is not the place to rehearse those arguments.
Stranger still: Rome herself routs Anabaptists from Scripture — Bellarmine boasts his baptism arguments cannot be escaped (On Baptism 1.9).
The same Bellarmine, attacking Scripture's sufficiency, then says paedobaptism cannot be proved from Scripture.
We appeal from partisan Bellarmine to Bellarmine elsewhere convinced by the truth.
